themes.theme: US midterms and Iran diplomacy risk premium
themes.summary: Democratic sweep and diplomatic signals led front-month Brent and WTI to the lowest since Aug. 31 on Nov. 4 (Brent -$8.98/b), with partial rebound Nov. 5 as analysts debated escalation versus a deal.
Hormuz transits stayed near 19-21 a day versus an October average of 25 amid mine and attack reports; NYK assumes closure through March 2027 and CERA sees exports below pre-war through 2027.

themes.theme: Atlantic Basin and North Sea oversupply
themes.summary: Dated Brent differential fell to -$2.885/b, lowest since May 2020, as high freight shut Asia arbitrage and WTI Midland, CPC and West African cargoes overhung NWE.

themes.theme: Weak Middle East and Asian crude demand
themes.summary: Dubai cash-futures spread fell from about $21/b in Sept to $8/b in Oct and 30 cents/b on Nov. 2, with ample offers, unsold cargoes and Asian refinery run cuts.

themes.theme: Strong refining margins, tight product stocks
themes.summary: Majors posted refining margins of $42-$50/b, China suspended gasoil exports with stocks at the lowest since 2023, and Ukrainian strikes put nearly 47% of Russian refining offline per CERA.

themes.theme: US crude into Asia and freight economics
themes.summary: Japan, Korea and India sharply raised US crude imports, but WTI Midland premiums to Dubai remain elevated at $31.50/b and easing VLCC, Suezmax and Aframax rates are reshaping the arbitrage.
Permian Resources, APA, Matador and Murphy raised 2026 guidance, while Cenovus, CNR, South Bow and PDVSA (1.23 million b/d in Oct) signalled higher Americas output.
